claims.text: The coupled tribo-corrosion behavior of the high-entropy alloy is governed by the kinetics and mechanical integrity of its passive oxide film during sliding.
Minor Al alloying enhances passivation by forming a stable Al2O3-enriched film.
An Al2O3-enriched film suppresses wear-accelerated corrosion by maintaining a self-healing protective layer.
An Al2O3-enriched film suppresses mechanical material removal by maintaining a mechanically intact protective layer.
The proposed baseline is mirror-polished, air-passivated, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The intervention is addition of 5 at% Al to produce (CoCrFeMnNi)95Al5.
The controlled test uses reciprocating sliding against an Al2O3 ball in 3.5 wt% NaCl at 25 °C, 5 N, 1 Hz, and 10,000 cycles.
Passive-film thickness, composition, and adhesion mediate the effect of Al addition on tribo-corrosion.
Al promotes rapid formation and repair of an Al2O3-rich oxide layer during wear.
The Al2O3-rich layer is mechanically robust under the stated sliding conditions.
Rapid oxide repair reduces exposure of fresh metal.
Reduced fresh-metal exposure limits localized corrosion and mechanical wear.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, the Al-modified alloy will decrease total mass loss by approximately 30%–50%.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, the Al-modified alloy will decrease wear volume by approximately 30%–40%.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, the Al-modified alloy will decrease steady-state corrosion current by approximately 50%.
The predicted reductions indicate diminished wear-corrosion synergy.
The prediction holds in near-neutral chloride environments at moderate sliding loads below 10 N when passive-film regeneration can compete with removal.
The prediction fails at extreme loads where passive-film removal outpaces reformation.
The prediction fails under purely abrasive, nonoxidizing conditions where the passive film cannot reform.
The magnitude of improvement depends on Al content and tribo-corrosion test parameters.
